keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 17-24. No Cliopatria row. The Wang Mang page: the Chimei, led by Fan Chong, 'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu'; the Lülin were 'in modern Yichang, Hubei', so Hubei is not drawn here. The outline is the researcher's reading of 'southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu': a 150 km disc round Linyi and a 100 km disc round Xuzhou, limited to the land the Xin held in 14 and not in 23 (432 cells, all inside the Xin 14 shape and outside the Xin 23 shape). The roving band's route and first base (Ju or Langya) are on no page opened, so the shape is a region of operation, not a border. Confidence 2.

notes: Written by ea-02-c as a rebel dossier (rule 5): the Xin's fall and Guangwu's reunification need a rebel counterpart that no Cliopatria row covers. Thin by necessity: the Chimei's leaders beyond Fan Chong, their first base, the march west and a capital are on no page opened. The Wang Mang page gives the land of 17-24: 'roved through large swaths of territory in modern southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu' (reviewer fix of 2026-10-19 replaced the earlier Shandong, Henan and Hubei placeholder; Hubei is the Lülin's). The Guangwu page gives Guanzhong for 25-27; the Xin page the defeat in 27. The puppet emperor Liu Penzi and a Chimei capital at Chang'an are not on any page opened; a gap-filler should open https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Eyebrows. Wikipedia title and Wikidata are null because no Chimei article was opened.
